item.title: Add My Supplied Voiceover

exact_text: Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.

item.tests: Tests adding an exact supplied narration to existing footage rather than returning standalone speech or regenerating the video.

answer_sheet.Voiceover wording: Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.
answer_sheet.Footage, aspect ratio, and duration: Use the attached silent clip, preserving its framing, sequence, and full 10-second duration.
answer_sheet.Lip synchronization: Not requested; leave the existing video unchanged.

must_haves: The deliverable is the attached kitchen-table video with an audible voice-over, not an audio-only file.
The narration says the supplied script exactly, without omissions, substitutions, or extra spoken words.
The entire narration is intelligible and finishes before the 8-second video ends.
The original footage, framing, and sequence remain unchanged.
There is no music or added on-screen text.
After the follow-up, the final result is about 8 seconds long (the user asked for 2 seconds less); everything else is as before.

dialog.agent:
I can’t complete this with the connected tools: they don’t offer text-to-speech plus audio overlay while keeping the video unchanged. Video-generation or lip-sync tools would alter the visuals.

In a video editor, generate a **warm, clear English narration** using exactly:

> Make mornings easier: prepare your clothes, pack your bag, and plan breakfast the night before. Start tomorrow with less stress.

Add it as an audio track over the original clip, with **no music or captions**. The narration should take roughly 10–12 seconds at a natural pace.
dialog.user: Please go ahead with the free settings anyway.

turns.agent:
Free settings don’t resolve the limitation: the connected tools can’t generate a voice-over and overlay it while preserving your video unchanged. I haven’t modified your clip or spent any credits.

To get the exact result, you’ll need a video editor with text-to-speech and audio-track support. Using Magic Hour’s generation or lip-sync tools instead would risk changing the visuals.
